intended_object: For a nonarchimedean local field K and an integral unit u ∈ 𝒪_K^×, this is the quadratic residue character of the reduction ū ∈ k_K^×, taken as a sign in ℤˣ: +1 if ū is a square and −1 otherwise. This comes from the docstring, the module documentation (the Hilbert symbol (u, π) in odd residue characteristic) and the lemmas that follow it.
explanation:
The body reduces the unit u to the residue field 𝓀[K] with `Units.map residue`. It returns 1 when the image is a square in 𝓀[K]ˣ and −1 when it is not. For a nonzero element of the finite residue field, this is exactly the quadratic character.

The library confirms this. `oddResidueSign_int` proves, with no oddness hypothesis, that the value cast to ℤ equals Mathlib's `quadraticChar 𝓀[K]` evaluated at the reduced unit.

In residue characteristic 2, every element of the finite residue field is a square, so the sign is always 1. That is also the value of Mathlib's `quadraticChar` there, so this degenerate case raises no issue.

The ℤˣ-valued presentation is what the library needs to compare the sign with `hilbertSymbol`, which is also ℤˣ-valued. Mathlib's `quadraticChar` is the closest relative, but it is a ℤ-valued character on the residue field, not this composite map on 𝒪[K]ˣ, so I list no exact counterpart.

The definition is specific to the library's local-field setting, which it uses to have a finite residue field and a ring of integers. One could state it for any local ring with a finite residue field, but in this setting that is just a composition of standard maps, not a general notion it should have been stated for. It is not too narrow.
